### Session 1 | topic: CRISPR off-target prevalence is assay-dependent | reading date: 2015
[s1_t1] Researcher: Let us start a new thread. My working hypothesis is: A guide RNA's off-target risk can be characterized by a single absolute genome-wide number. What does the literature say?
[s1_t2] Assistant: GUIDE-seq (cell-based, integration tag) reports many sites; (source: no single source)
[s1_t3] Assistant: CIRCLE-seq (in vitro, sensitive) reports more candidate sites with high false-positive risk; (source: no single source)

### Session 2 | topic: CRISPR off-target prevalence is assay-dependent | reading date: 2015
[s2_t1] Researcher: Continuing the CRISPR off-target prevalence is assay-dependent thread. What does the newer literature add?
[s2_t2] Assistant: DISCOVER-seq (in vivo, MRE11 ChIP) reports fewer high-confidence sites; (source: no single source)
[s2_t3] Assistant: CHANGE-seq layers chromatin context on CIRCLE-seq. (source: no single source)

### Session 3 | topic: CRISPR off-target prevalence is assay-dependent | reading date: 2015
[s3_t1] Researcher: Continuing the CRISPR off-target prevalence is assay-dependent thread. What does the newer literature add?
[s3_t2] Assistant: The 'true' off-target set differs by assay; reconciliation requires assay metadata. (source: no single source)
[s3_t3] Researcher: Any methodological caveat I should record for this thread?
[s3_t4] Assistant: Noted for the record: Same gRNA, four assays, four answers - clean method-dependency arc. Easy 15+ QA: count differences, threshold sensitivity, in vitro vs in vivo, chromatin effect.

### Session 4 | topic: Single-cell RNA-seq batch correction - no universal best method | reading date: 2018
[s4_t1] Researcher: Let us start a new thread. My working hypothesis is: A single batch-correction algorithm is appropriate for all scRNA-seq integration tasks. What does the literature say?
[s4_t2] Assistant: MNN (Haghverdi 2018) and Seurat v3 anchor-based integration (Stuart 2019) introduced popular integration methods. (source: cb07_p1, cb07_p2)
[s4_t3] Assistant: Reference cb07_p1 is Haghverdi et al. 2018, Nat Biotechnol 36(5):421-427 (MNN), "Batch effects in single-cell RNA-sequencing data are corrected by matching mutual nearest neighbors" (2018).
[s4_t4] Assistant: Reference cb07_p2 is Stuart et al. 2019, Cell 177(7):1888-1902 (Seurat v3), "Comprehensive Integration of Single-Cell Data" (2019).

### Session 5 | topic: Single-cell RNA-seq batch correction - no universal best method | reading date: 2020
[s5_t1] Researcher: Continuing the Single-cell RNA-seq batch correction - no universal best method thread. What does the newer literature add?
[s5_t2] Assistant: Tran 2020 and Luecken 2022 both found that different methods win in different scenarios; no universal best method exists, and performance depends on cell-type composition imbalance and the trade-off between batch removal and biological conservation. (source: cb07_p3, cb07_p4)
[s5_t3] Assistant: Reference cb07_p3 is Tran et al. 2020, Genome Biol 21(1):12, "A benchmark of batch-effect correction methods for single-cell RNA sequencing data" (2020).
[s5_t4] Assistant: Reference cb07_p4 is Luecken et al. 2022, Nat Methods 19(1):41-50, "Benchmarking atlas-level data integration in single-cell genomics" (2022).
[s5_t5] Researcher: Any methodological caveat I should record for this thread?
[s5_t6] Assistant: Noted for the record: Clean 'no single best' arc. Strong for benchmarking-knowledge QA and method-tradeoff reasoning. Expert note: Stuart 2019 is Seurat v3 anchor-based integration, not pure CCA.

### Session 6 | topic: AlphaFold2 accuracy on disordered regions and conformational ensembles | reading date: 2021
[s6_t1] Researcher: Let us start a new thread. My working hypothesis is: AlphaFold2 produces accurate structures for any protein sequence. What does the literature say?
[s6_t2] Assistant: Jumper 2021 reports CASP14-level accuracy for many ordered protein domains. (source: cb04_p1)
[s6_t3] Assistant: Reference cb04_p1 is Jumper et al. 2021, Nature 596(7873):583-589, "Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold" (2021).

### Session 7 | topic: AlphaFold2 accuracy on disordered regions and conformational ensembles | reading date: 2021
[s7_t1] Researcher: Continuing the AlphaFold2 accuracy on disordered regions and conformational ensembles thread. What does the newer literature add?
[s7_t2] Assistant: Ruff & Pappu 2021 is the clean IDR-specific source: low pLDDT often marks disorder rather than ordinary structural error. (source: cb04_p3)
[s7_t3] Assistant: Reference cb04_p3 is Ruff & Pappu 2021, J Mol Biol 433(20):167208, "AlphaFold and Implications for Intrinsically Disordered Proteins" (2021).

### Session 8 | topic: AlphaFold2 accuracy on disordered regions and conformational ensembles | reading date: 2022
[s8_t1] Researcher: Continuing the AlphaFold2 accuracy on disordered regions and conformational ensembles thread. What does the newer literature add?

[s8_t3] Assistant: Reference cb04_p2 is Akdel et al. 2022, Nat Struct Mol Biol 29(11):1056-1067, "A structural biology community assessment of AlphaFold2 applications" (2022).

### Session 9 | topic: AlphaFold2 accuracy on disordered regions and conformational ensembles | reading date: 2022
[s9_t1] Researcher: Continuing the AlphaFold2 accuracy on disordered regions and conformational ensembles thread. What does the newer literature add?
[s9_t2] Assistant: Saldano 2022 shows conformational-diversity limits: AlphaFold often converges to one conformer even where multiple experimentally known states exist. (source: cb04_p4)
[s9_t3] Assistant: Reference cb04_p4 is Saldano et al. 2022, Bioinformatics 38(10):2742-2748, "Impact of protein conformational diversity on AlphaFold predictions" (2022).
[s9_t4] Researcher: Any methodological caveat I should record for this thread?
[s9_t5] Assistant: Noted for the record: Headline claim is right but scope-bounded. Useful for teaching scope/condition reasoning rather than contradiction. Expert note: do not describe Akdel as only IDR-focused; distinguish IDRs from conformational diversity.

### Session 1 | topic: EZH2 / PRC2 - context-dependent oncogene vs tumor suppressor | reading date: 2002

[s1_t3] Assistant: Reference cb08_p1 is Varambally et al. 2002, Nature 419(6907):624-629, "The polycomb group protein EZH2 is involved in progression of prostate cancer" (2002).

[s2_t4] Assistant: Reference cb08_p4 is Beguelin et al. 2013, Cancer Cell 23(5):677-692, "EZH2 Is Required for Germinal Center Formation and Somatic EZH2 Mutations Promote Lymphoid Transformation" (2013).

### Session 3 | topic: EZH2 / PRC2 - context-dependent oncogene vs tumor suppressor | reading date: 2010
[s3_t1] Researcher: Continuing the EZH2 / PRC2 - context-dependent oncogene vs tumor suppressor thread. What does the newer literature add?
[s3_t2] Assistant: Ernst 2010 reported inactivating EZH2 mutations in MDS/MPN - loss-of-function pathogenic in myeloid disease. (source: cb08_p3)
[s3_t3] Assistant: Reference cb08_p3 is Ernst et al. 2010, Nat Genet 42(8):722-726, "Inactivating mutations of the histone methyltransferase gene EZH2 in myeloid disorders" (2010).

### Session 4 | topic: EZH2 / PRC2 - context-dependent oncogene vs tumor suppressor | reading date: 2010
[s4_t1] Researcher: Continuing the EZH2 / PRC2 - context-dependent oncogene vs tumor suppressor thread. What does the newer literature add?
[s4_t2] Assistant: EZH2 is therefore lineage-context-dependent: same gene, opposite roles. (source: no single source)
[s4_t3] Researcher: Any methodological caveat I should record for this thread?

### Session 4 | topic: Cellular senescence markers - no single specific marker | reading date: 2015
[s4_t1] Researcher: Let us start a new thread. My working hypothesis is: p16INK4a expression alone reliably identifies senescent cells in tissue. What does the literature say?
[s4_t2] Assistant: Sharpless & Sherr 2015 reviewed marker landscape and noted p16 expression in non-senescent contexts (immune cells, stem cells). (source: cb09_p1)
[s4_t3] Assistant: Reference cb09_p1 is Sharpless & Sherr 2015, Nat Rev Cancer 15(7):397-408, "Forging a signature of in vivo senescence" (2015).

### Session 5 | topic: Gut microbiome composition and obesity (Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio) | reading date: 2016
[s5_t1] Researcher: Continuing the Gut microbiome composition and obesity (Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio) thread. What does the newer literature add?
[s5_t2] Assistant: Sze & Schloss 2016 reanalysis of 10 studies found F:B differences were small and not reliably reproducible - the textbook claim no longer holds at population scale. (source: cb03_p4)
[s5_t3] Assistant: Reference cb03_p4 is Sze & Schloss 2016, mBio 7(4):e01018-16, "Looking for a Signal in the Noise: Revisiting Obesity and the Microbiome" (2016).
[s5_t4] Researcher: Any methodological caveat I should record for this thread?
[s5_t5] Assistant: Noted for the record: Textbook claim that became contested. Excellent for an evolving-hypothesis arc with explicit refutation. Method scope: cohort heterogeneity, primer choice, taxonomy bins. Expert note: keep mouse mechanistic energy-harvest claims distinct from human population F:B-ratio claims; this host-context dependence is part of the arc.

[s7_t1] Researcher: Continuing the BRCA1 missense variants - saturation genome editing reclassification thread. What does the newer literature add?

### Session 8 | topic: BRCA1 missense variants - saturation genome editing reclassification | reading date: 2018
[s8_t1] Researcher: Continuing the BRCA1 missense variants - saturation genome editing reclassification thread. What does the newer literature add?
[s8_t2] Assistant: Method-as-evidence: how a high-throughput assay reshapes a clinical claim. (source: no single source)
[s8_t3] Researcher: Any methodological caveat I should record for this thread?
[s8_t4] Assistant: Noted for the record: Uncertainty-resolved-by-method arc. Good for QA on what 'evidence' means and why the prior 'unknown' answer was correct at the time. Expert note: Plon 2008 and Richards 2015 are classification frameworks; Findlay SGE plugs into them. This is uncertainty resolved by a new method, not contradiction.

### Session 9 | topic: Cellular senescence markers - no single specific marker | reading date: 2019
[s9_t1] Researcher: Continuing the Cellular senescence markers - no single specific marker thread. What does the newer literature add?
[s9_t2] Assistant: Gorgoulis 2019 international consensus: senescence requires multi-marker evidence (SA--gal + p16/p21 + SASP + proliferation arrest), no single marker is sufficient. (source: cb09_p3)
[s9_t3] Assistant: Reference cb09_p3 is Gorgoulis et al. 2019, Cell 179(4):813-827, "Cellular Senescence: Defining a Path Forward" (2019).
[s9_t4] Researcher: Any methodological caveat I should record for this thread?
[s9_t5] Assistant: Noted for the record: Definition-evolved arc - the field operationally redefined senescence to a multi-marker requirement. Good 'what counts as evidence' QA. Expert note: treat Gorgoulis 2019 as a field-defining consensus statement; p21/CDKN1A is a common companion marker to p16.
